messages:
maya: heads-up — acme-support opened an escalation: intermittent partial responses + duplicate billing after client reconnects to our SSE endpoint. They say reconnects sometimes resume mid-chunk and the client then replays the rest, causing duplicated tokens billed.

acme-support: repro steps we got from the customer: long generation (~10s), network hiccup -> client reconnects immediately, sends same request without waiting for resume confirmation. Sometimes output shows overlapping fragments.

devon: can you paste an example of the client-side logs? curious about whether they're reusing an idempotency key or creating a fresh one on reconnect.

acme-support: here's abridged client log they sent:
```
[10:12:05] -> POST /v1/streams?model=gpt-x
[10:12:06] SSE: data: {"type":"delta","seq":201,"session":"sess-99","text":"...the results are"}
[10:12:07] connection reset by peer
[10:12:07] reconnecting...
[10:12:08] -> GET /v1/streams/resume?session=sess-99
[10:12:08] SSE: data: {"type":"resume_ack","cursor":"cur-55","seq":201}
[10:12:08] -> POST /v1/streams?model=gpt-x (new request, no idempotency-key)
[10:12:09] SSE: data: {"type":"delta","seq":202,"session":"sess-100","text":" are pretty good"}
```

maya: interesting — they requested resume but then started a fresh POST immediately. That matches duplicates. We should confirm server resume ACK semantics and whether we guarantee dedupe when a new request arrives with overlapping sequence numbers.

liam: quick note: our resume ACK currently provides a cursor and last_seq but we treat incoming new POSTs as independent unless client attaches the resume cursor or idempotency key. For safety we could accept either: 1) client uses resume flow (GET resume then continue on same session) OR 2) client replays same POST but with idempotency-key we can detect identical intent. If they do neither, we can't reliably dedupe.

sse-bot: deploy 2026-03-08T14:02Z -> prod (serving-runtime v4.8.1)

devon: for this customer, they said their SDK auto-retries POST on any disconnect and does not carry over idempotency-key. That's the root cause. But the weird bit is the partial overlap — they sometimes *do* get a resume ack and then still receive another stream that contains the tail which they've already received prior to the disconnect. Could be race between resume ACK and queued deltas.

maya: can we reproduce quickly? steps I'd try: 1) start long generation with server; 2) after first delta(s), kill TCP connection client-side; 3) immediately open new connection and 3a) call resume endpoint, 3b) simultaneously POST new request. See which messages we emit to client.

liam: i ran a local repro with a small harness. Observed race: resume handler emits resume_ack (cursor + last_seq) but there can be in-flight deltas still being flushed to socket goroutine; if those flushes were retried on the old socket they get lost — new connection then starts delivering an overlapping sequence under a new session id. This leaves the client with partials from both sessions.

devon: logs from our side (trimmed):
```
[14:03:10] session sess-99: started; seq=200
[14:03:11] stream: emitted delta seq=201
[14:03:12] conn: reset (client tcp tear)
[14:03:12] resume_handler: resume request for sess-99 -> cursor cur-55 last_seq=201
[14:03:12] flush-loop: attempted flush on old socket failed; enqueue for retry
[14:03:12] new_session sess-100: started; seq=202
[14:03:12] resume_ack sent for sess-99
[14:03:12] queued delta 201 delivered on new_session sess-100
```

liam: the core issue is we don't atomically swap the in-flight buffer when a resume occurs; queued deltas may be delivered under a new session id without reconciliation. That results in duplicate or partial overlap on the client.

maya: that aligns with the customer's report. Also billing: if meter counts per-token emission event and we count across sessions independently, duplicated tokens are billed twice. We need a short-term mitigation and a longer-term fix.

devon: quick mitigations we can propose to customer: a) recommend client pause-before-retry: wait for resume_ack or a short backoff (200-500ms) before issuing a new POST; b) attach idempotency-key on retry so server can dedupe identical requests; c) upgrade SDK to propagate resume_cursor so they can continue same session instead of new POST.

acme-support: they asked for a reproducible script they can run to validate — can we provide one?

liam: here's a minimal curl/node repro they can try (unofficial):
```
# step 1: start generation (client A)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams -d '{"model":"gpt-x","prompt":"long..."}' &
# simulate network hiccup: kill that process after some bytes
# step 2: immediately try resume
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/resume?session=sess-99" &
# step 3: immediately POST new request without idempotency-key
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams -d '{"model":"gpt-x","prompt":"long..."}'
```

maya: for the internal fix: we should ensure resume flow drains and merges in-flight buffers atomically and implement server-side idempotency matching for near-identical POSTs within a short window (e.g., 5s) keyed on model+prompt+user+input-hash. That avoids billing dupes even if client retries.

devon: agree. also patch to billing: detect token duplicates across sessions if they map to same resume_cursor or same idempotency-key within time window; mark duplicate tokens as not billable and emit a billing-adjustment event. That can be used for customer credit.

liam: i'll open a runtime bug: "sse: in-flight buffer not reconciled on resume -> overlapping deltas" and add test harness. i'll also add a short-lived feature flag to enable strict resume gating (blocks new POST until resume completes) for a canary.

maya: please also capture steps to offer acme a temporary workaround and offer a bill credit if we detect repeated duplicates. acme-support, can you confirm how many customers affected?

acme-support: only acme-corp reported so far, but they have 3 prod services. they want a repro script and a timeline.

maya: ok — devon/ liam, target: patch queued for next patch window, and a KB message for SDK users recommending idempotency-key + resume_wait. I'll draft the customer message and include the quick repro and mitigation.

devon: ping me once you have the repro script and the patch PR. i'll run billing checks and surface any credits needed.

liam: PR link will follow. putting notes in the bug. :eyes:

maya: thanks all. I'm going to DM acme-support the repro + suggested immediate config changes (client backoff + idempotency).

sse-bot: incident-note: created issue #INF-7122 referencing this thread
